newsitem.title: USA: Jesse Helms faces U.S. election advertising war.
newsitem.headline: Jesse Helms faces U.S. election advertising war.

text.p: Conservative Jesse Helms has a 10 percentage point lead in his bid to hold his Senate seat against the challenge of Democrat Harvey Gantt, opinion polls show, in a race that is becoming increasingly bitter.

Helms, 74, the head of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, six years ago held off Gantt to win a fifth term in a racially charged contest where Helms prevailed by a 53 percent to 47 percent margain.
"You get into October and the shots become harder and more difficult," University of North Carolina political science professor Thad Beyle said.

Voters decide Nov. 5 whether they will be represented by Helms, whose record is dominated by anti-communism and opposition to abortion and gays; or Gantt, a two-time mayor of Charlotte with a pioneering civil rights history and a reputation for coalition building.

Helms leads Gantt 50 percent to 40 percent in the most recent Mason-Dixon poll, but political analysts caution the survey may be flawed because many telephones were out of order in the wake of Hurricane Fran.
In his latest television ad, Helms told voters Gantt has promoted homosexuality, favours same-sex marriages and is more liberal than President Bill Clinton.
"Harvey Gantt says, quote, 'I can offer no objections to same-sex marriage,'" an announcer says as the same words are superimposed over a picture of Gantt in the ad.
"Harvey Gantt ... too liberal for North Carolina," it says.
Gantt retaliated with an ad calling Helms a liar.

"His ads are the same old lies. Harvey Gantt opposes gay marriages," an announcer says as Gantt is shown surrounded by his wife of 32 years, children and grandchild. "He believes in the traditional family," it ends

The Helms campaign says the ad stems from a 1995 interview Gantt gave the gay and lesbian newspaper "Q Notes." But in the interview Gantt said, "I don't feel good about same-sex marriages," adding that from the standpoint of public policy he had no objection to allowing homosexuals the same benefits as married couples.
Gantt, 53, wants to debate Helms, who has declined. "He can't defend his record to the voters, so he's hiding behind these attack ads," Gantt said in a speech.
Helms' campaign maintain he has no need to debate because voters know who he is and where he stands.
